When externalCalendarId is falsy, the find can never match (externalId is a non-empty string), so the fallback yields undefined, unlike the old behavior which used the destination calendar's externalId. Same dead fallback appears in deleteEvent. The mechanism is verifiable directly from the diff lines.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `updateEvent` now sets `selectedCalendar` as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the else-branch), the `.find()` predicate compares `cal.externalId` to a falsy value (`undefined`/`null`), which will not match real externalIds, yielding `undefined`. The same pattern is applied in `deleteEvent` (`calendarId = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`). This is a diff-introduced logic error that can cause updates/deletes without an explicit `externalCalendarId` to target an undefined/incorrect calendar (or fall back incorrectly elsewhere), potentially leaving stale events.
